passage:
Sunday night.
Hafsa's reply is still sitting there: "ok. hope the concert was fun." No emoji. Hafsa ALWAYS uses emojis. I cancelled her birthday dinner on Friday because Faraz got me a spare concert ticket, and I told myself she'd understand, she has lots of friends. Now there's a sick sort of guilt in my stomach. But also, honestly? Part of me wants to message her: "Come on, it was a once-in-a-lifetime thing, you'd have done the same." Would she? I don't know. Ammi raised me to be the kind of man who shows up. I keep opening the chat and closing it.
— Noor

qa.a: It said "ok. hope the concert was fun." with no emoji.

qa.q: What is Noor feeling as he keeps opening the chat?
qa.a: He feels a sick sort of guilt, mixed with a wish to defend himself by calling the concert a once-in-a-lifetime thing. 😔

qa.q: What turning point is available to Noor right now?
qa.a: He could skip the defensive message and admit plainly that cancelling Hafsa's birthday dinner for a concert let her down.

qa.q: What might Hafsa's missing emoji tell Noor about how she feels?
qa.a: Since Hafsa always uses emojis, the plain reply hints that she is hurt and cool toward him, though it is a cue, not proof.

grounding: Shows a young man who cancelled a friend's birthday for a better offer feeling a pang of guilt at her cold reply, mixed with an urge to defend himself.

Vidya: saw the photos from Sid's rooftop party btw
(Raghav stared at the screen. His face went hot.)
Raghav: ok that was like one hour
Raghav: I was going to come after
(He deleted the last line.)
Raghav: ...
Vidya: it's fine
(It clearly wasn't fine. He felt a pang in his chest. He had picked a party over her birthday dinner, and right now he wanted to explain it away more than he wanted to say sorry.)

qa.q: Where did Vidya see photos from?
qa.a: She saw the photos from Sid's rooftop party.

qa.q: What does Raghav want more than to say sorry?
qa.a: He wants to explain it away, even though he feels a pang of guilt about picking the party over her birthday.

qa.q: What could Raghav send instead of excuses?
qa.a: A plain acknowledgment: "I chose the party over your birthday. That wasn't fair to you, and I'm sorry."

qa.q: What does "it's fine" likely mean from Vidya?
qa.a: Vidya is probably hurt and guarded; "it's fine" is a short way of saying she isn't ready to talk.

grounding: Shows a young man realising, from his friend's cold replies, that skipping her birthday for a party hurt her, with guilt mixed with a wish to defend himself.
